World.title: Difficult to believe Putin would meet CIA chief, says Ex-ISS director
World.content:
Former Internal Security Service Director General Arnold Sinisalu said the head of the U.S.' Central Intelligence Agency's visit to Russia this week does not necessarily mean a secret agreement is being made and it is worth remaining calm.

On Tuesday, it was reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe had unexpectedly flown to Moscow via Latvia. U.S. media wrote that he held talks with Russian officials, but the subject of the discussions is unknown.

The last time the head of the U.S. intelligence agency visited Moscow was a few months before Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. The Americans wanted to make it clear to the Russians that their plans were known and to advise them to stop.

Sinisalu, now a visiting professor at the University of Tartu's Johan Skytte Institute, told Vikerraadio's "Uudis+" program on Wednesday that communication between the services of two major powers is normal and could cover many topics, not only Ukraine.

"We should not think that the only issue between Russia and America is the war in Ukraine," he said. Sinisalu said the military conflict between Iran and America may be the top priority, as it also affects U.S. domestic politics.

Sinisalu said if the U.S. had wanted to keep the visit completely secret, it could have done so. "They could have changed planes several times," he explained.

Additionally, the ex-general director said there is no reason to fear that the two countries are making secret agreements with each other, because the level of trust between them is low.

However, the large aircraft on which Ratcliffe flew to Russia should be looked at separately. He explained that both the FBI and CIA chiefs generally use smaller aircraft to travel. Sinisalu concluded that there must be something on board the aircraft or that it is a matter of security.

Prisoner exchange?

"There has been speculation about many different things here, including whether this is a prisoner exchange," he said. Sinisalu noted that this would seem the most logical explanation. At the same time, prisoner exchanges have been carried out much more quickly and have sometimes even been shown live. "We should take this calmly and proceed from the assumption that it is probably something with much simpler content," he said.

Sinisalu added that the CIA director has generally not traveled to Russia in person for prisoner exchanges, but said there could be something accompanying it. "For example, last-minute bargaining over someone that can only be decided at the very highest level, excluding the presidents," he explained.

The former director general said the question is rather how broad a spectrum of issues the major powers discussed. "U.S. intelligence certainly has various pieces of information that are being used in attempts to start Ukraine-Russia negotiations or resolve the situation with Iran," he said.

Sinisalu noted that there has recently been a great deal of speculation about whether Russia is planning some kind of operation against the Baltics or NATO. He said that Russia currently does not have the strength to carry out a frontal attack in the sense of conventional warfare. "That would also be foolish, because it would give the Ukrainians an excellent opportunity to launch a counterattack, since Russia simply does not have the manpower or weaponry," Sinisalu said.

Developments in space should not be forgotten either. "There has been talk of certain satellites monitoring European and American satellites," Sinisalu noted.

Remain calm

The U.S. newspaper The Wall Street Journal reported that Ratcliffe may also have met with President Vladimir Putin to deliver some kind of warning to him. The U.S. has gathered intelligence indicating that Russia is making preparations for a possible mobilization and also plans to test NATO's resolve.

Sinisalu said that Putin generally does not meet with officials of this kind. "Some kind of message may be relayed there, but I find it difficult to believe that he would physically meet with him," he noted.

Sinisalu said talk of testing NATO is psychological pressure aimed at keeping people in Europe anxious and creating domestic political turbulence.

"Some small special forces provocation is possible, but a large-scale war would be seen coming, and NATO's land, sea and airspace along the borders is monitored very closely," he said, adding it is worth remaining calm.

Sinisalu noted that since the meeting did not take place covertly, it cannot be called a secret meeting.

World.title: Expert: Center Party leader can't stop his MPs voting in presidential election
World.content:
Kõlvart, who is not a Riigikogu member, said earlier in the week that his party would not be voting in the Riigikogu ballots next Wednesday and Thursday, as there is no alternative candidate to Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise.

"A party chairman cannot forbid any member of the Riigikogu from taking part in a presidential election. At this point, I would recommend that Mihhail Kõlvart read the Constitution," political expert Annika Arras told ERR's "Otse uudistemajast" on Wednesday.

The fact that there is only one candidate registered to run – Madise, who was signed off on by 75 MPs where only 21 are needed – along with the process generally over the summer, has raised questions again about the way in which Estonia elects its president.

The head of state is not directly elected by the people, but by the Riigikogu in the first instance, passing to a regional electoral college if this draws a blank. This system was put in place to avoid undue outside interference in the election of the head of state.

Arras said direct presidential elections would certainly be much more exciting than the current vote at the Riigikogu. "In that case, candidates would have a reason to travel around Estonia, present themselves and talk to the people. There would be considerably more opinion polls than there are today," she said.

Also, the issue of outside interference applies to Riigikogu and local elections too, Arras noted, though these enfranchise all Estonian citizens – plus all EU citizens in the case of local elections. "In reality, there is no really watertight argument as to why [the president] could not be directly elected, but it is a matter for discussion and a question of choices. I would be fine with either option," she went on.

The transparency or culture of the presidential elections is ultimately up to the politicians and their actions, she noted; amending the electoral system would not change that on its own. At the same time, Arras noted, another criticism of the process this time around and at past presidential elections is how last-minute the formal nomination of candidates is, or even their public presentation.

"If we altered it so that candidates got nominated earlier, we asked them questions, held debates right here at the public broadcaster and at other media outlets, then politicians would make their choice and people would have a much better idea of whom parliament is electing," she went on.

As for why Isamaa swung the balance further by getting behind Madise last week, Arras said most likely Madise impressed at her meeting with the party's Riigikogu faction – potential candidate Tiit Land had also met with the party before that – and this convinced Isamaa she would be a good head of state.

Also, it might have been difficult to stem a flood of support for Madise from individual Isamaa MPs and others – as Kõlvart has been trying to do with his party.

"This in turn demonstrates that presidential elections in Estonia are so important to every member of the Riigikogu personally that the classic party discipline often used with different parliamentary votes is not easy to maintain," Arras added.

Annika Arras appearing on 'Otse uudistemajast'. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

The Conservative People's Party of Estonia (EKRE) simply cracks down on dissenters by expelling them, but this rigid discipline is likely behind their ongoing marginalization, Arras went on, noting that recovery can and does happen too. EKRE put forward party founder Mart Helme as presidential candidate, but lacked enough seats at the Riigikogu to register him on their own.

One further consideration is the March 2027 Riigikogu elections. Arras said the parties that backed Madise will score political points if she does get elected president, particularly the Social Democrats (SDE), who were the first to publicly endorse Madise.

"But I believe that, overall, all those who have now rallied behind Ülle Madise will benefit in any case," she added, noting that the office of president continues to carry a high degree of public trust.

With four of the six Riigikogu parties backing Madise, the presidential elections are unlikely to prove decisive come March, Arras went on. "There are still five or six months to go until the parliamentary election, which means that anything can still happen. The election results have not been decided today."

Recent opinion polls put Madise's rating with the public as high as 43 percent.

Kõlvart: Party still deciding how to act at presidential election

Kõlvart on Wednesday denied that members of the Center Party faction are prohibited from participating in the Riigikogu vote on Madise September 2-3, adding the party has not yet decided how exactly it will vote on that day.

He reiterated that there had been no debate on Land as an alternative candidate.

"We proceed based on the principle that a party should have a consistent and comprehensible policy and position. From the very outset, we have expressed the view that there should be a broader debate, and to do that you need more than one candidate. We have also expressed our support for Tiit Land. There has been no debate; we have only one candidate," Kõlvart told ERR.

This means the party still sees the situation as less than ideal, he went on. "The Riigikogu group will still decide how we express our position. But in our view, the process we are seeing now is not right, and we also do not believe it is right to take part in it."

The true issues cannot be revealed if a candidate runs unopposed, the Center chair continued. "A debate would show that. It is not possible to say on the basis of one meeting. That is why, in our view, there should have been genuine competition and a debate lasting longer than one day, so that not only the Center Party but society as a whole would have a broader understanding of what the vision of one candidate or another actually means."

The current Riigikogu composition does not reflect public support, he added, reiterating his party's support for direct presidential elections. Madise's election as head of state would remain "an appointment" and not an election, he added, noting that Madise's meeting with the Center Party did not prove sufficient to determine her suitability; a proper debate over a longer period would have been needed, he said.

Overall, the past two months has been little more than a "performance," with spectators looking on to see if Madise would run, or not.

At the last presidential election in 2021, Alar Karis ran unopposed and was voted in after the second ballot. Karis announced in mid-summer he would not be seeking re-election, even though he is eligible for a second term.

World.title: Up to 400 children without school places, says education minister
World.content:
Minister of Education Kristina Kallas (Eesti 200) believes between 300 and 400 children will be missing from the school system by mid-September as Estonia introduces compulsory education until the age of 18.

From this academic year, Estonia has raised the age of compulsory education to 18 years old, meaning all children must attend high school. However, discussions have arisen in recent weeks about the lack of school places.

When a student is marked missing from the school system, it means the state or local government cannot contact them and does not know where they are.

The minister told ETV's morning program "Terevisioon" on Tuesday that many students have not submitted high school applications. This is partly due to students returning to Ukraine for the summer, but some Estonian children have also disappeared from the system.

However, students who have submitted applications have also not received places.

Kallas said holding students back a year to repeat 9th grade is not an option in many cases, especially if they have not received sufficient support throughout their school years.

"These students need a different learning environment, teachers and approach, and preparatory studies are intended precisely for children who have such significant learning gaps or health problems that they need completely different support from what they have received at school so far," she explained.

Kallas also disagreed with teachers that preparatory studies will actually help solve the problem.

Critical situation in Tallinn

Kallas said that the situation is currently most critical in Tallinn. "A child with grades slightly below average can no longer get into any school," she said.

The number of children from outside the capital applying to study in Tallinn has also been higher than average. This has taken places away from local students, she said.

Kallas said that all Tallinn upper secondary schools are currently full, but admissions are still ongoing at almost all of them. This means that students are constantly moving from one school to another.

"Places are turned down again, places become available again. You have to constantly be on the lookout for where places become available," the minister explained. She said this is very stressful and the system should be reviewed.

Karl Erik Kirss, chairman of the board of the Estonian School Student Councils' Union, said it is important that students without a place get clarity on the situation and should be allocated a point of contact from the state or local government.

Kirss explained that many students, particularly non-Estonian-speaking students, are currently uncertain about how their studies will continue on September 1.

"On Tuesday, we instructed our state schools in Tallinn that if a student comes in who appears unlikely to cope even in vocational education because, for example, they do not speak Estonian at all, they should be officially registered as a candidate for preparatory studies," Kallas said.

She explained that this would allow the ministry to know how many additional preparatory study places the state needs to commission.

Vocational schools a viable alternative

Kallas said that new curricula have been launched in vocational education over the past two years.

Significantly more young people are entering vocational education this year than in previous years. "It has become significantly more attractive," she added.

The minister noted that over time, vocational education will become a fully viable alternative after basic school.

Kirss said that the new curricula in vocational education help change students' perception that vocational school is somehow a worse choice than upper secondary school.

"Of course, the current situation, where upper secondary school places are full and all students without a school place are being directed to vocational schools, probably reinforces the perception that vocational school is still a second choice," he added.

The minister said Tallinn College of Technology has more than 400 vacant study places. "If you are interested in the field of technology, then you should definitely contact that school in Tallinn," she added.

If it turns out that there is no suitable study path there after all, the information will be forwarded to the Education Ministry and the ministry can deal with the child individually. "If upper secondary school places are needed, then in Tallinn they are predominantly provided by the city, and in that case the Education Department should be contacted," Kallas said.

World.title: Painting conservator: Soviet‑era artists had to paint with whatever materials they could get
World.content:
Polina Richter, a painting conservator at Kumu art museum who is researching Soviet‑era oil‑painting materials for her master's thesis, says that the scarcity of supplies in that period forced artists to invent creative solutions.

Richter is studying in the master's program in heritage protection and conservation at the Estonian Academy of Arts and is currently writing her thesis. Her research focuses on the materials used in Soviet‑era oil paintings — specifically the peculiarities of material use at the time and how artists obtained what they needed.

Richter said artists working during the Soviet period mainly got their materials from the Artists' Union shop. Quantities were limited, and artists were often allocated a fixed amount of specific paints. "Many came up with quite interesting solutions because of the lack of materials," she said.

She has not heard of artists making their own pigments when supplies ran out. "But certainly someone may have gone that far," she added.

Dentist tools in the conservator's toolbox

Richter's work at Kumu centers on preparing paintings for exhibitions. Many works have already been conserved, but some were restored decades ago and need to be reassessed before being shown again.

"Unfortunately, time does its work, so they need a bit of touching up again for the exhibition," she said.

Richter compares painting conservation to treating a patient. First, the conservator must determine the artwork's history and current problems, then choose the appropriate methods to address them.

Kumu's painting department has four staff members. The museum also has departments for paper, sculpture and frames. Workload varies throughout the year — autumn and spring are busier because more exhibitions are prepared then.

Before an exhibition, conservators assess which works need preparation and whether there is enough time to restore them all. The job also involves working closely with curators, storage staff and other museum employees.

Removing old varnish not always a necessity

A conservator's toolbox includes chemicals, primers and paints. "One of the most interesting things conservators use are actually dentist tools — something you wouldn't expect, but they're great for picking and doing fine detail work," she said.

Every intervention must be carefully considered. For example, removing old varnish is a decision conservators discuss thoroughly.

"Varnish is generally part of the painting. Since varnish yellows over time and undergoes various changes, you have to look very carefully at whether it should be removed at all," Richter explained.

If the materials of a work are not well known, tests are done before starting. Samples may be examined under a microscope or sent to a lab if needed.

Unexpected situations can arise during conservation. "These are usually accidental and human. They don't happen often, but the team tries to find solutions. And since we're conservators, we have to fix them ourselves," she said.

World.title: Court rejects request by convicted traitor for early release
World.content:
Harju District Court ruled on Tuesday that it will not grant convicted traitor Deniss Metsavas's request for early release under electronic monitoring.

The Prosecutor's Office does not support Metsavas's conditional early release, and the prosecutor maintained that position during the hearing. Tallinn Prison likewise does not support allowing the inmate to continue serving his sentence under electronic monitoring supervised by a probation officer.

Metsavas's defense argued that through his conduct and efforts, he has shown that he has drawn the necessary conclusions from his crimes and that continued imprisonment is not strictly necessary to guide his behavior.

When deciding on conditional early release, the court considers the circumstances of the crime, the offender's personality and prior life, behavior during imprisonment — including participation in activities that reduce the risk of reoffending or willingness to participate in such activities during supervision — as well as living conditions and the potential consequences of early release.

The court reviewed the submitted materials, written opinions from the prosecutor and defense, and heard the prosecutor, the convict and his attorney. Based on this, the court concluded that early release would be premature and unjustified.

The court agreed with the defense that Metsavas has several positive factors supporting early release: a stable place to live, supportive family members, vocational training completed during imprisonment, work in various positions such as librarian and instructor of math and yoga groups, no unpaid claims, and savings in his release fund.

However, the court noted that these positive factors alone do not guarantee lawful behavior after release. Metsavas also had a job, home, family and supportive relatives before imprisonment, yet still committed serious crimes.

The main substantive condition for early release is a reliable forecast that the inmate will behave lawfully in the future. Despite the positive aspects, the court considers the risk of reoffending to be high.

This assessment is supported by the seriousness of Metsavas's first‑degree crime, committed over a long period. In the court's view, the risk of new offenses has not been sufficiently reduced.

The ruling has not yet entered into force.

The court convicted Metsavas of treason in 2018 and sentenced him to 15 years in prison.

World.title: Systematic thefts jump 25% in first half of year
World.content:
Compared with other crimes, systematic thefts grew the fastest in the first half of this year, Justice Ministry says. They were registered a quarter more often than during the same period last year.

A systematic theft is a petty theft committed at least three times within a short period. Most of these are shoplifting cases.

Mari‑Liis Sööt from the Ministry of Justice said this rise in systematic thefts is not unique to Estonia. The same trend is troubling Europe more broadly, where shoplifting and organized retail theft have reached their highest levels in decades.

"If we look at Finland, the UK and several other countries, theft numbers have increased there as well," Sööt said.

Mari-Liis Sööt. Source: Ministry of Justice

As for why theft has increased, she said we can only speculate. One reason may be that the cost of living has risen.

"Criminal networks have also become more professional. Interpol and Europol say this," Sööt added.

Taivo Rosi from the Tartu Police Department said repeated petty thefts have kept police busy for years. It is difficult to claim they have suddenly surged.

"In grocery stores, people pay for part of their goods and leave some items unscanned. When such reports reach the police, it becomes clear fairly quickly that this is no longer a case of customer forgetfulness but intentional behavior — a kind of invoice optimization. They pay for the cheaper goods, leave the expensive ones unscanned at self‑checkout and walk out of the store with a straight back and a proud face," Rosi said.

Politsei. Autor/allikas: Martin Dremljuga/ERR

According to him, people still steal the same things as before: expensive food and alcohol from grocery stores, and costly construction and gardening tools from hardware stores.

"We can also mention the well‑known light vehicles and bicycles, which the police have been talking about for years," Rosi added.

Ministry of Justice statistics show that a total of 14,600 crimes were registered in the first half of the year — a six‑percent increase compared with last year.

World.title: Estonian defense company to invest €200 million in Latvian plant
World.content:
Wolfram Europa will invest €200 million to build an explosives and warhead manufacturing complex near Jēkabpils, Latvia, with production set to begin in 2027, the company announced Wednesday.

The 40-hectare facility will be built on land secured under a long-term agreement with Latvia's State Forests (LVM). Construction and production are planned in three phases beginning in 2027, with around 200 skilled jobs expected once the complex is fully operational.

Wolfram Europa said the plant will produce military explosives, warheads and counter-mobility systems. At full capacity, it is expected to produce up to 300 metric tons of RDX or 100 metric tons of HMX annually, as well as assemble 100,000 anti-tank mines and 200,000 warheads per year.

Latvian Economics Minister Viktors Valainis said the investment would strengthen the country's defense industry while creating high-value jobs and increasing industrial capacity.

Wolfram Europa CEO Magnus-Valdemar Saar said the Jēkabpils facility would be the company's first major production site as it seeks to expand explosives manufacturing capacity in Europe.

The company said in its press release that Europe is producing far from enough explosives and that it aims to fill that gap. Its goal is to become Europe's largest explosives manufacturer.

"Over the past 35 years, Europe has steadily scaled back its explosives and ammunition industry, which has also brought technological development in the sector to a standstill. Europe is rearming, but investment remains focused primarily on platforms and final assembly. This is the explosives gap: weapons production is being scaled up faster than the explosives and warheads that make those weapons effective," Saar said.

World.title: Iraq’s central bank denies issuing banknotes with three zeros removed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) officially denied reports that it has issued new banknotes with three zeros deleted.

The CBI said in a statement that allegations of producing new currency denominations are unfounded and have no official source.

Any future plans to redenominate the currency or eliminate zeros must go through extensive legal, regulatory, and technical processes, according to the statement.

The CBI urged citizens and media outlets to rely solely on official channels to avoid public misunderstanding and market speculation.

Lawmakers and government officials have lately discussed ideas to remove three zeros from the Iraqi dinar to return stockpiled currency to the legitimate banking system and combat corruption.

According to Jamal Kocher, a Kurdish member of the Iraqi parliament’s finance committee, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has asked for the removal of zeros from invoices.

Kocher told The New Region that if the plan is implemented, 1,000 Iraqi dinars would be converted to one dinar, while 25,000 dinars would be equivalent to 25 dinars.

Earlier in August, Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad acknowledged the plan to eliminate the zeros and modify the currency.

Despite public discussion and declarations, the CBI has yet to publish a clear timeframe or complete a plan for any currency reform.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate against Iraqi dinar continues to fall
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar continued to decline on Wednesday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate dropped in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,539.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,545 Iraqi dinars and 1,535 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate declined, fluctuating between 1,539.5 and 1,539 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq’s financial revenues decline by 42% in June 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s federal budget revenues plummeted to roughly 35.94 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $27.45 billion) in June 2026, down from 62 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $47.3 billion) during the same month in 2025, marking a 42 percent decline.

According to budget figures, the income generated from oil exports in June 2026 reached 28.5 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $21.76 billion), compared to 57.05 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $43.57 billion) in June 2025, representing a decline of around 28.54 trillion Iraqi dinars ($21.79 billion).

The country’s non-oil income climbed to almost 7.44 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $5.68 billion) in June 2026, up from 4.95 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $3.78 billion) in June 2025.

Oil’s proportion of overall revenues decreased from 92 percent in June 2025 to 80 percent in June 2026, while the contribution of non-oil revenues to the country’s budget climbed from eight percent to 20 percent.

The World Bank’s ‘Global Economic Prospects’ report, published in June 2026, highlights Iraq as a developing economy that relies significantly on commodity earnings, especially oil.

The World Bank has cautioned about the effects of commodity price volatility on the financial and economic stability of energy-exporting countries.

Commodity prices have been vulnerable to periodic shocks since the start of the current decade, the most recent being the huge disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict, which resulted in dramatic swings in global markets for oil, metals, and agricultural supplies.

Iraq’s economic output grew by 0.5 percent in 2024; however, according to estimates, it contracted by 1.5 percent in 2025 before continuing its downward trajectory in 2026. It is expected to rebound to a 12.2 percent growth rate in 2028.

The World Bank mentioned that Iraq’s economy is one of the most vulnerable to regional developments, with its growth forecast lower compared to several other Middle Eastern oil-producing countries.

World.title: Iraq’s Gulf Keystone revenue unchanged as oil prices balance output decline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Gulf Keystone Petroleum, the operator of the Shaikan field, one of the largest developments in Iraqi Kurdistan, reported stable revenue during the first half of 2026.

The company’s revenues hit $82.8 million as higher oil prices balanced a 67 percent decline in output due to instability in the region.

The company’s shares rose by 9.6 percent following increased revenues and reduced operating costs.

The company’s revenues are nearly unchanged compared to $83.1 million in the first half of 2025.

Adjusted financial operating profitability increased by 26 percent to $51.7 million, driven by cost reduction and robust pricing.

The firm plans to increase output safely and begin a water handling project in the first quarter of 2027.

The Shaikan field is one of the largest oil fields discovered in the Kurdistan region of Iraq and serves as Gulf Keystone Petroleum’s principal asset.

The field covers around 280 square kilometers and is located about 60 kilometers northwest of Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan’s capital.

The oilfield has an estimated 416 million barrels of proven reserves. It has been in commercial production since 2013.

World.title: President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council visits Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, Faiq Zaidan, paid a high-profile, one-day official visit to Tehran on Tuesday to boost cross-border legal cooperation, develop bilateral judicial agreements, and address important security concerns.

Zaidan met with Iran’s senior executive, legislative, judicial, and security leaders, including the Iranian president, minister of justice, judiciary chief, speaker of the parliament, and secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.

The meetings focused on aligning judicial protocols and managing shared legal issues, strengthening legal relations, streamlining judicial procedures, activating cooperative security frameworks, reviewing legislative support for cross-border law enforcement, and addressing border stability and security measures.

Zaidan strongly opposed the foreign economic pressure against Iran, citing the latest US sanctions imposed under “Operation Economic Outcast.”

The Iraqi judicial chief indicated that Iraq will never forget Iran’s support during the US war against the country in 2003 and the war against ISIS terrorist groups.

Zaidan called for the full execution of existing bilateral legal and security agreements between Baghdad and Tehran.

The Iraqi official added that it is important to enhance intelligence cooperation, curb smuggling networks, streamline extradition protocols, and tackle the existence of anti-Iran groups along shared borders.

World.title: 30 Iraqi students join PetroChina Scholarship at China University of Petroleum
World.content:
Qingdao/ Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Thirty Iraqi university students are completing their preparatory semester at the China University of Petroleum (East China) in the coastal city of Qingdao, marking the inaugural cohort of the Pioneers of Excellence academic scholarship program.

The initiative represents the first time the Iraqi federal government has mobilized the state Training, Technology Transfer, and Scholarship Fund (TTSF) to sponsor undergraduate engineering scholars in China. Funded under the corporate social responsibility and capacity-building commitments of PetroChina Iraq – West Qurna 1, the program bridges bilateral energy development with engineering education.

The scholarship follows a customized “0.5 + 4” academic curriculum designed specifically by China University of Petroleum (East China):

Preparatory Foundation (6 Months): Intensive Mandarin Chinese language acquisition paired with foundation courses in advanced calculus, physics, and chemistry.

Undergraduate Degree (4 Years): Full Bachelor of Science degree tracks focusing on three core upstream disciplines: Petroleum Engineering: Reservoir management, well completion, and enhanced oil recovery (EOR). Mechanical Engineering: Industrial machinery design, refinery turbines, and pipeline hydraulics. Petroleum Geology: Geophysical seismic surveying, structural sedimentology, and basin modeling.



Selected through nationwide competitive examinations and panel interviews organized jointly by the Ministry of Oil and the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, the students represent diverse Iraqi governorates.

Bilateral Diplomatic Patronage: During the program’s official inauguration ceremony in April, the Consul General of China in Basra, Chen Peizhong, and the Scientific and Educational Counselor at the Iraqi Embassy in Beijing, Dr. Mohanad Najah Jawad Al-Shorofi, addressed the cohort, highlighting the importance of developing native technical talent to lead Iraq’s domestic energy sector.

Student Commitment: Class representative Mohammed Al-Tawous reaffirmed the students’ commitment to mastering advanced engineering curricula to support the modernization of Iraq’s oil and gas infrastructure upon graduation.

Industrial Synergy: Since assuming the role of lead contractor at the giant West Qurna 1 oil field in 2024, PetroChina has prioritized local workforce upskilling, transitioning bilateral energy ties from traditional equipment procurement to joint human capital development.

Hydrocarbons form the foundation of Iraq’s national economy. By equipping domestic engineering talent with advanced training at premier international energy institutions, the Ministry of Oil aims to build a modern technical workforce capable of operating complex extraction assets, deploying artificial lift technologies, and managing next-generation energy infrastructure across southern oil fields.

World.title: Iraq and South Korea finalize financing for air defense missile system
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Minister of Finance Falih Sari met on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, with the South Korean Ambassador to Iraq, Lee Jae-myung, to finalize the financing mechanisms for the contracted air defense missile system between Iraq and South Korea.

The high-level meeting was attended by the Chief of Staff of the Iraqi Army, General Staff Officer Abdul Amir Rashid Yarallah, alongside the South Korean military attaché in Baghdad, according to an official statement issued by the Ministry of Finance and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Key Financial & Operational Discussions

Contractual Financial Framework: The talks focused on operationalizing the payment schedules, legal frameworks, and treasury mechanisms required to fulfill bilateral contractual commitments without procedural delay.

Airspace Sovereignty Mandate: Minister Sari emphasized that securing Iraq’s airspace and modernizing territorial air defense capabilities remain national priorities to protect state sovereignty and critical infrastructure against external airborne threats.

High-Level Military Coordination: The presence of General Staff Officer Yarallah underscores operational synchronization between the Ministry of Defense’s procurement timetable and the Ministry of Finance’s budgetary disbursements.

Bilateral Commitment: Ambassador Lee Jae-myung and the South Korean defense attaché reaffirmed Seoul’s commitment to expediting technical execution and delivery timelines in line with agreed bilateral protocols.

The air defense procurement contract with South Korea represents a major technological leap for the Iraqi Air Defense Command.

By securing multi-tiered surface-to-air missile interception batteries, Baghdad aims to establish full sovereign control over its national airspace, replace legacy systems, and build an integrated radar and missile shield capable of intercepting advanced airborne threats, drones, and ballistic targets.

World.title: Chief Justice Zaidan and U.S. Envoy discuss post-coalition arms control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The President of Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Dr. Faiq Zaidan, received the Chargé d’Affaires of the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Joshua Harris, on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, to discuss judicial mechanisms and the enforcement of the rule of law following the scheduled conclusion of the International Coalition’s military mission.

According to an official statement issued by the Supreme Judicial Council and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the discussions focused on legal procedures regarding entities and individuals bearing arms in violation of the Iraqi Constitution and applicable laws, as well as institutional frameworks to enforce the rule of law universally across the country.

Key Discussion Pillars

Post-Coalition Legal Framework:Reviewing judicial and legal preparations ahead of the formal conclusion of the Global Coalition against Daesh/ISIS mission in Iraq on September 30, 2026.

Prosecution of Unregulated Arms:Outlining judicial measures against groups and individuals possessing, displaying, or utilizing unauthorized weapons outside the direct chain of command of state constitutional institutions.

Universal Rule of Law:Establishing judicial coordination mechanisms to ensure that legal statutes and constitutional provisions apply equally to all entities without exception.

The meeting comes as Iraq prepares for the transition of the U.S.-led international military mission into bilateral security partnerships.Restricting weapons exclusively to state custody remains a core pillar of the Iraqi government’s institutional program.

By coordinating judicial procedures alongside executive security measures, the Supreme Judicial Council aims to reinforce national sovereignty, enhance judicial oversight over armed actors, and solidify internal stability as the international military mandate concludes.

World.title: Over 61,000 wait for kidney transplants
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India faces a widening gap between demand for kidney transplants and the availability of donor organs, with 61,668 patients on the waiting list, nearly five times the number of kidney transplants performed as of Feb 9, a parliamentary standing committee has said.

The committee on health and family welfare has recommended that kidney transplant facilities be expanded to at least three govt medical colleges in large states and one in every small state and UT, besides setting time-bound targets to increase organ retrieval centres and transplant infrastructure, particularly in underserved and hilly regions.

India performed 11,558 living-donor and 1,918 deceased-donor kidney transplants in 2024, while 61,668 patients remained on the waiting list as of Feb 9.

The committee â in its report tabled in the recently concluded monsoon session of Parliament â said the figures highlight the widening mismatch between demand and capacity and the continued dependence on living donors.

It said transplant activity remains concentrated in a handful of states and metropolitan centres, including Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka, leaving access uneven across the country.

The committee attributed the shortage partly to Indiaâs low deceased-organ donation rates, citing social misconceptions, inadequate awareness, limited organ retrieval infrastructure and procedural bottlenecks. It has called for a nationwide behavioural-change campaign and stronger hospital-based organ retrieval and transplant coordination systems.

Data from the National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation for 2019-23 showed that women constituted 63.8% of living organ donors, while men accounted for 69.8% of transplant recipients. The committee has sought a study to determine whether socioeconomic, cultural, financial or gender-related barriers contribute to the disparity.

World.title: Dissidents push for Hindu Pradesh Congress Committee chief to end Punjab crisis
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress is again mulling the idea of appointing a Hindu state president in Punjab amid a push from dissidents for a compromise to end the turmoil in the state unit.

Well-placed sources said the deadlock in the dissidence-ridden organisation has cast a cloud over the upcoming election campaign, and the party brass is cut up about the unsuccessful fire-fighting efforts of key managers.

A group of dissidents that includes senior netas like

and Sukhjinder Randhawa has been seeking the replacement of state chief Amarinder Raja Warring ever since the AICC announced a clutch of poll-related panels while sticking with Warring at the helm two months ago.

Now, sources said, the dissidents themselves have proposed that a Hindu Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) chief be appointed. This group has also conveyed that they will be on board with such a replacement, even though each one of them has been fancying their chances till now, they added.

With the state chief and the leader of opposition both belonging to the Jatt Sikh community, the idea of a Hindu PCC chief is meant to bring balance to the organisational set-up.

This was the original idea before the AICC decided to retain Warring at the top.

An insider said the party is looking at its options and may have to make some change in the leadership position â either the Punjab chief or AICC in-charge, or both. While it is too close to the elections for such an organisational overhaul, the sources said the crisis has to be defused.





Sources also dismissed the notion that Rahul Gandhi will soon kickstart the state campaign in the form of a bus journey, arguing that the bus would bring all the squabbling netas together and, thereby, enforce peace.

It swept away settlements, hydropower units and the pilgrim route.Nepal Police put the toll at 157, while Chinese authorities reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibetâs Gyirong county. Nepal Police said 579 others â 466 foreigners from 28 countries and 113 Nepalis â remained untraced, including at least 133 Indians. Among the missing were at least 37 NRIs. Frighteningly, as many as 33 bodies were found 150km downstream at Chitwan, showing how far the dea-dly waters carried victims.Among the missing foreigners were 54 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 Britons, 24 Canadians, 19 Malaysians and 8 Koreans.Many were Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims, with nearly 400 of them, including the Indians, preparing to cross the Nepal-Tibet border or travelling through the region when the flood struck.Rescue personnel battled poor weather, mud, washed-out roads and high river levels even as authorities moved families from vulnerable settlements to safer locations.Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal told parliament that 29 police personnel and 44 soldiers remained untraced after floodwaters swept away their barracks in Rasuwa, while customs officials, hydropower workers and other employees stationed near the border were also missing. At the 20MW Langtang Khola Hydropower Project, dozens of workers are out of contact. The torrent also swept away or inundated security posts, customs facilities, banks and other establishments along the river corridor. Nepal PM Shah appealed for patience and unity as the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force deployed helicopters, drones, boats and ground teams for search-and-rescue operations.Across the border, floods and mudslides severed several roads, communications and electricity around the (dry) Gyirong port, a key Nepal-Tibet crossing used by Kailash-Mansarovar pilgrims. Chinese president Xi Jinping called for âall-out efforts to search and rescue people who are missingâ.The flood destroyed critical infrastructure across northern and central Nepal, with preliminary govt estimates showing at least 19 bridges and around 40 km of roads damaged or washed away; 13 hydropower projects were hit, and around 200 trucks were lost. The Nepal govt declared the worst-affected areas disaster-hit zones for the next 3 months and ordered authorities to provide free treatment to the injured.

World.title: UN panel report on minorities is politically motivated: Govt
World.content:
'Politically motivated, highly malicious': India denounces UN racial discrimination committee remarks

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has rejected as politically motivated and highly malicious observations made by a UN committee on the alleged targeting of minority communities and Rohingya refugees.UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination had âhighlightedâ in a report the increase in law enforcement operations targeting âRohingya, Bengali-speaking Muslims, migrants and asylum-seekers, particularly following the 2017 home affairs order and the April 2025 Pahalgam attack in Kashmirâ.Ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, âIndia rejects any politically motivated, highly malicious references in the report with all the contempt that it deserves.âTaking note of the press release issued by the committee after Indiaâs periodic review, the ministry said this was a routine âtreaty-bodyâ review, and India had participated in the spirit of constructive engagement. The official also said Indiaâs commitment to combating racial discrimination remained unwavering.Govt had highlighted Indiaâs âconstitutional safeguards, robust legal framework, pluralism and sustained efforts to protect disadvantaged communitiesâ.âWhile we will respond to the committeeâs observations through the established procedure, the inter-ministerial delegation, which was led by solicitor general Tushar Mehta, had already rejected the sweeping generalisations, unsubstantiated allegations or tendency to exceed the conventionâs mandate during the review meeting,â said the official.âOur mission in Geneva had already issued a detailed press release following the review,â he added.

World.title: 3 lakh tonnes of refined sugar to enter market
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In what could improve availability of sugar in the market immediately and bring down prices, around 3-3.5 lakh tonnes available with Indian sugar refiners, who import raw sugar duty-free and export it after processing, is likely to come into the domestic market following a recent govt decision.

Last week, govt had allowed duty-free import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar and also allowed the processors to sell some refined sugar, which was meant for export only, in the domestic market. Officials and industry insiders said at least 3 lakh tonnes of processed sugar could come into the market quickly. The subsequent import of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will help tide over any supply issue.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Meanwhile, the ex-mill price of sugar has gone down by 20% in the past 10 days.

Industry sources and officials said the ex-mill price in Kolhapur fell to Rs 48 per kg Wednesday and was around Rs 53 a kg in Uttar Pradesh.

An official said ex-mill prices increasing from Rs 48 per kg to Rs 58-60 per kg in just a few days showed that speculation and stocking were the main reasons behind the price spike, and there had been no shortage.

Deepak Ballani, director general of Indian Sugar Mills Association, the countryâs top sugar industry body, said that govt measures to rationalise sugar prices had started showing results. âOver the last few days, ex-mill sugar prices have declined by nearly 20%, and we expect this reduction to be reflected in retail prices very soon. There is adequate availability of sugar in the country, and consumers will get the commodity at reasonable prices during the forthcoming festive season,â he added.

On Wednesday, the average retail price of sugar was Rs 65 per kg.

World.title: Nepal flash floods LIVE: At least 157 dead, hundreds missing; India sends first tranche of relief materials
World.content:
At least 157 people were confirmed dead and more than 400, including around 133 Indians, were missing or out of contact after a massive flash flood in Nepal’s Bhotekoshi River swept through villages in Rasuwa, a district bordering China’s Tibet region, on Wednesday morning, authorities said.

Also read | At least eight killed in Nepal flash flood; multiple districts placed on high alert

“Several security personnel, government officials and employees of hydropower projects are also out of contact,” the PMO said. “The disaster has damaged 19 motorable bridges and 40 kilometres of road.”

Officials said the death toll could rise and that it would take days to assess the full extent of the damage.

Also read | At least 50 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu stranded as landslips disrupt route

Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a social media post that he was left with a “heavy heart”. “The entire nation has been left shocked and deeply saddened by the loss of life and damage to property,” he added, describing the disaster as “sudden” and “massive”. Stating that the government immediately mobilised all its resources for rescue operations, he vowed that rescue operations would continue through the night.

World.title: Tahir Hussain moves Delhi HC against conviction in IB officer’s murder case
World.content:
Former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) councillor Tahir Hussain has approached the Delhi High Court challenging his conviction and life sentence for the murder of Intelligence Bureau (IB) officer Ankit Sharma during the February 2020 riots in north-east Delhi.

The appeal, which was filed on August 24, is likely to come up for hearing next week.

“The investigation against the appellant has been tainted since the very beginning, aimed at implicating him in order to satisfy public anger. The FIR is ante-dated and ante-timed, no material investigation was carried out until March 6, 2020, that is, till the appellant was arrested in another case,” Hussain contended.

He alleged that some witnesses were planted while statements of genuine eyewitnesses were “manipulated”, adding that the actual perpetrators have not been brought to book.

Hussain sought the setting aside of the trial court’s July 13 conviction order and July 31 sentencing order, contending that the trial court believed the statements of completely “unreliable witnesses” and relied upon those who did not witness the incident while ignoring the “tainted investigation”, including fabrication of the complaint on which the FIR was based.

On July 31, the trial court sentenced Hussain and four co-convicts — Nazim, Qasim, Javed and Anas — to life imprisonment for the IB officer’s murder. While the prosecution had sought the death penalty for all the accused, the court observed that the case did not fall within the “rarest of rare” category warranting capital punishment.

World.title: Nepal flash flood: T.N. pilgrims stranded in Nepal; officials coordinating steps to rescue them
World.content:
At least 57 pilgrims, as per available information, from Tamil Nadu were among the Indians who were stranded in Nepal, where flash floods left behind a trail of destruction on Wednesday (August 26, 2026).

Nepal flash floods live updates

While a group of 21 have reached out to officials seeking rescue, steps were taken to locate the rest of the party, as of 8.30 p.m. IST.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay expressed shock over the devastating flash floods in Nepal, in which several Indians, including people from Tamil Nadu, were missing. He also ordered speedy and coordinated efforts to find and rescue people from the State and provide them with necessary assistance. In a post on X, he said he had ordered officials at Tamil Nadu House in New Delhi to coordinate the rescue operation.

The State government also announced round-the-clock toll-free helpline numbers for family members to coordinate with officials. According to an official release from the Department of Welfare of Non-Resident Tamils, family members could contact the helpline numbers. The helpline number within India is 1800 309 3793. Those calling from abroad can give a missed call to +91 80690 09900 or contact +91 80690 09901. Those who want to reach the control room at the Tamil Nadu House in New Delhi can contact 92895 16712.

The 57 pilgrims went to Nepal on a tour organised by a Kumbakonam-based company in tie-up with a Nepal-based company. They landed in Nepal a few days ago and were heading towards the Tibet border as part of their travel plan when the mishap took place. Divided into three groups, they travelled in three buses to Tibet border, sources said.

Nepal floods: PM Modi speaks to Balendra Shah, offers humanitarian assistance

“Along with them, two others from Maharashtra too joined them. The incident happened around 8 a.m. today. Occupants of one of the vehicles took refuge on top of a hill,” a source coordinating rescue efforts said, adding that it is not immediately known as to what happened to the occupants of the other two vehicles.

While about 21 of them managed to get shelter at a Nepal border police outpost, the status of others was yet to be ascertained, according to an official spokesperson of the travel company. Meanwhile, the Thanjavur, Tiruvarur and Mayiladuthurai district administrations have started collecting the addresses and other details of the tourists from their respective districts and were perusing the condition of tourists with the Central government, official sources said. 11 persons from Chidambaram and Bhuvanagiri in Cuddalore district are among the pilgrims from Tamil Nadu who have been stranded in Nepal.

Founder of Isha Foundation Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) evening said that of the 21 groups who are part of their sojourn, 495 people have already returned safely, while 743 people were currently in Tibet, 148 people were in Nepal, and 77 people were at the immigration center and three volunteers in Timure, Nepal.

“All of us, including the volunteers and support teams are deeply anguished and are doing our utmost to assist in the rescue. There has been no official information on the whereabouts of any of the people who were at the immigration office. We are working with the authorities to see if we can get to the location and stand ready to be part of the rescue efforts, regardless of the risk involved,” he said in the post.

T. Sugumar (71) of Mayiladuthurai, whose wife, S. Manimekalai (64), had gone on a tour on Sunday (August 23, 2026) from Chennai to Kailash, said that his wife had communicated on Wednesday (August 26, 2026), saying that she was safe somewhere near the Nepal border. There were 19 others, along with Ms. Manimekalai, who travelled in the same vehicle on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) before the incident was reported.

“The call from my wife came around 11 a.m. to our daughter, saying that she and others were safe, said Mr. Sugumar. Where she was staying could not be known immediately. She could not be contacted thereafter, he further said.

Another traveller from Mayiladuthurai district was Pushpalatha (60) of Kazhukaanimattam. Her relative Ramesh said Ms. Pushpalatha made a WhatsApp call in the morning saying that she was safe. After the incident was reported, we called the official helpline number to be told that Pushpalatha was safe, Mr. Ramesh said.

A couple Rathinakumar (65) and Poonguzhali (61) of Mayiladuthurai had also gone for the Kailash tour on Sunday. “We got a call and a message from my uncle who had accompanied my parents during the tour saying that they were all safe after the landslide got reported”, said R. Arun Bharat Ram - the son of Rathinakumar and Poonguzhali.

My parents called my sister thereafter to say that they were all safe in a camp, Mr. Arun Bharat Ram said, adding that his parents had embarked on a 14-day tour. “We could not contact them later because of communication problems, he said.

(With inputs from Coimbatore, Cuddalore and Tiruchi).

World.title: Trump declares emergency over foreign equipment in U.S. power grid
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump declared a national emergency on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) over foreign-made equipment inside the country’s electric grid, saying the growing need for power has made the system a target for hostile governments.

The executive order blocks companies from buying, importing or installing certain foreign-made parts used in what the government calls the bulk-power system.

A bulk-power system is the network of high-voltage lines, substations and power plants that transmits electricity across the country.

In the order, Mr. Trump said the boom in AI data centres and other advanced technology projects has left the United States more dependent on stable electricity than ever.

If the grid went down, he argued, the damage would be far worse than in the past.

The order also warns that foreign-built equipment could contain hidden digital “backdoors” in its software — secret access points that would let another country control or shut off the equipment.

The order applies to countries under U.S. arms embargoes or sanctions, or governments the administration decides are working against American interests.

China is not named, but Chinese-made grid parts have worried U.S. security officials for years.

Washington has used a similar playbook before, pressing allies to keep Huawei and fellow Chinese telecom supplier ZTE out of new mobile phone networks and arguing that Beijing could force the companies to spy or sabotage.

Both were later blacklisted by U.S. regulators.

World.title: FDA suspends license of popular Mumbai food establishment Ayub’s after finding houseflies, unsanitary workplace
World.content:
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the food license of Ayub’s in Fort on August 23, 2026, after finding food-safety violations, along with those of three other establishments in Mumbai and Nagpur, while taking separate action against food products in Pune, Jalgaon and Nagpur.

The FDA also inspected 37 hotels, restaurants and dhabas, issued improvement notices to 31 establishments and suspended the licenses of four food establishments, and approximately 60,709.8 kg of stock worth ₹2,24,61,888 was seized.

Ayub’s was inspected on August 22, 2026, when officials found extensive food safety flaws, including a lack of required temperature control facilities for food items, improper storage of high-risk food items like eggs at room temperature, and failure to properly segregate and store raw and cooked food items.

The facility’s food-handling area was also unclean, with open and poorly maintained drains, stagnant water at food-handling spots, houseflies in the area, and a lack of pest control measures and necessary personal hygiene facilities for food handlers. Necessary testing of food items was not conducted, and there were also flaws in records and food traceability systems.

These gaps in the basic food safety control system of the establishment create a risk of microbial contamination, cross-contamination between raw and cooked food, and unsafe food reaching consumers. The FDA suspended the FSSAI license of Ayub’s restaurant starting August 23, 2026.

The food business license of Sankalp Mahila Audyogik Utpadak Sahakari Sanstha Maryadit, located at Wadia Estate in Kurla West, Mumbai, was suspended, and further legal and administrative action would be taken.

In Nagpur, the licenses of Burhampur Jalebi Centre in Pratap Nagar and Step In Restaurant at Law College Square were suspended following routine inspections after they were allegedly found to be violating hygiene and food-safety requirements under Schedule 4 of the Food Safety and Standards Regulations. The two suspensions followed the regular administrative process and were not immediate suspensions.

The FDA also seized 4,317 kg of food products worth approximately ₹7.27 lakh from Trimurti Enterprises in Wadaki, Pune, on August 24, which was allegedly operating without a valid food license or registration. The seized products included refined soybean oil, turmeric powder, toor dal and chana that were suspected to be substandard or improperly labelled. Samples have been sent for laboratory analysis.

At Zam Zam Kirana in Adawad, Jalgaon district, officials found 396.8 kg of loose refined soybean oil, which they suspected was adulterated. Samples were collected, and a final determination will be made after laboratory testing.

In another action in Nagpur, the FDA recorded 55,996 kg of roasted arecanut, valued at approximately ₹2.24 crore, at Gourish Agro Pvt. Ltd. in Kalamna. Inspection and further proceedings under the Food Safety and Standards Act are underway, the FDA said.

World.title: Trump says U.S. doesn't need Canada; America's economy says otherwise
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump says his country does not need Canada. But every day, roughly 4 million barrels of Canadian crude oil flow south, helping fuel American cars, trucks and airplanes and supply U.S. industry.

And oil is only the beginning.

Canada also supplies aluminum, potash to U.S. farms and parts for an auto industry built on both sides of the border.

“WE DON'T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!” Mr. Trump posted this week, repeating his long-running claim.

Yet Mr. Trump has imposed a 50% tariff on Canadian aluminium while acknowledging this week that the United States badly needs the metal.

“This country desperately needs aluminium,” Mr. Trump said. “We don't have it. We get it all from Canada for the most part, and we need it badly.” The contradiction underscores how deeply the two economies remain intertwined — and how much could be at stake if Trump's trade war reaches more of the energy, materials and supply chains that the US still relies on Canada to provide.

Canada is the United States' second-largest trading partner after Mexico and energy is at the heart of that relationship.

The two countries exchanged about $872 billion in goods and services last year. Canadian crude imports equal nearly 20% of total U.S. petroleum consumption, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, part of the Department of Energy.

Daniel Beland, a political science professor at McGill University, said Mr. Trump's claim that the United States does not need Canada is “absolutely false,” citing U.S. reliance on Canadian oil and natural gas and deeply integrated industries such as autos.

Much of Canada's crude flows to Midwest refineries built to process its heavy oil into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel.

Energy also explains much of the US trade deficit with Canada, which Mr. Trump frequently cites as evidence of an unfair relationship.

The White House this week portrayed the relationship in starkly negative terms, saying Canada had taken roughly $50 billion a year from the United States over the past decade. Much of that gap reflects U.S. purchases of Canadian energy, which helps power the U.S. economy.

And Canada's heavy crude typically trades at a discount to U.S. benchmark oil, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Energy more than accounted for last year's $48.3 billion goods deficit. Without energy, the United States would have run a trade surplus.

After trade talks collapsed last Friday (August 21, 2026), the U.S. imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods. The measures cover only about 5% of Canadian exports to the United States and exclude energy.

For now, using oil as a weapon in trade negotiations remains a remote possibility. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith opposes restricting energy exports, arguing that doing so would hurt her province.

But former Alberta Premier Jason Kenney said Canada should not rule out export taxes on oil, fuel or potash if Trump escalates further.

Such retaliation “would affect Republicans who drive F-150s and lay fertiliser on their farm fields,” Mr. Kenney said.

“They should be mindful that if they really want to escalate, it will not end well for the American economy two months before midterm elections,” he said.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford cited Canadian commodities as leverage, accusing Mr. Trump of “putting out fake news” about the United States not needing Canada.

He called potash used by U.S. farmers “one of the most powerful tools we have” and said Washington would have to turn to suppliers such as Russia if Canada redirected shipments.

Mr. Kenney stopped short of advocating an export tax, and Béland said such a move would probably be “a very divisive issue politically in provinces like Alberta and Saskatchewan”.

That underscores the limits of Canada's leverage: measures aimed at hurting US industries could also hurt Canadian producers and strain political unity at home.

Canada has long been the dominant foreign source of aluminum for the United States. Smelting the metal requires enormous amounts of electricity, giving hydro-rich Canada a major advantage.

Prime Minister Mark Carney told a New York business audience in May that Canadian aluminium exports to the U.S. are “the energy equivalent of 10 Hoover dams”.

American farmers are even more dependent on Canada for potash, a fertiliser essential to crops such as corn and soybeans. More than 80% of U.S. potash imports come from Canada.

Even Mr. Trump's ambassador has disputed the idea that the United States needs nothing from its neighbour.

“America has a tremendous amount of things where we have a need,” Ambassador Pete Hoekstra said in June. Pointing to Canadian fertiliser supplies, he added: “We need potash.” Then there are cars.

Canada and the United States have built an integrated auto industry in which parts can cross the border up to six times before final assembly, according to the Canadian government.

Mr. Trump said on Monday (August 24, 2026) that his administration would impose 50% tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks and auto parts starting Jan 1, 2027 — after the November midterm elections.

That means a tariff aimed at Canada can land in Michigan or Ohio. Tax Canadian aluminum and an American automaker may pay more for metal. Tax Canadian parts and the cost of assembling an American vehicle can rise.

Artificial intelligence is driving a surge in electricity demand. Canada supplied 85% of U.S. electricity imports in 2023, according to the Canada Energy Regulator, and Carney says the country needs to double the capacity of its electricity grid by 2050 through major hydroelectric and nuclear projects.

Mr. Carney said Canada could help the United States “meet exploding demand to power AI".

World.title: Indian Tea Association issues white paper on Darjeeling & Dooars Tea Industry seeks revival packages
World.content:
Seeking a revival and sustainable development of the tea industry in North Bengal, the Indian Tea Association (ITA) on Wednesday (August 26, 2026) published two white papers on the Darjeeling Tea Industry and the Dooars & Terai Tea Industry.

The Darjeeling White Paper, in particular, highlights the sharp decline in production—from 14.49 million kg in 1990 to 5.6 million kg in 2025—and calls for urgent, targeted intervention to safeguard the globally recognised GI heritage of Darjeeling Tea.

“The Darjeeling White Paper proposes an indicative annual financial support package of approximately Rs. 113 crore, covering areas such as orthodox tea production, working capital interest support, transport, mechanisation, social security support, rejuvenation and factory modernisation,” a press statement by ITA said.

The white paper on Dooars & Terai Tea Industry points out at a market asymmetry where small tea growers, who account for 68% of State production, operate without comparable statutory welfare obligations, while organised estates bear the full burden of housing, healthcare and compliance costs, creating a dual-cost environment that depresses auction prices and threatens the organised sector’s survival.

Over the past few weeks the representatives of ITA met State’s Industry Minister Tapas Roy, Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta and Advisor to Chief Minister Subrata Gupta.

“The White Papers comprehensively examine the structural, financial, climatic, labour and market-related challenges confronting these two iconic tea-growing regions and set out a roadmap of policy interventions aimed at restoring competitiveness, strengthening sustainability, protecting livelihoods and promoting long-term investment,” the statement from ITA said.

The association expressed hope that the white papers would facilitate continued dialogue with the State Government and lead to time-bound and coordinated policy interventions for the revival of the Darjeeling and Dooars–Terai tea industries.

World.title: SC youth’s death: CB-CID names six police officers as accused
World.content:
The CB-CID charge sheet filed in the Scheduled Caste youth Akash Delison’s custodial death case revealed that a murder case has been registered against six policemen, including a police inspector.

Delison, from Krishnarajapuram near Manamadurai in Sivaganga district, was arrested on March 5, 2026 in connection with a case in which two people were hacked during a dispute in Manamadurai. Delison was admitted to the Madurai Government Rajaji Hospital with injuries, but he died at the hospital.

The police had claimed that he was injured after falling from a bridge while trying to escape arrest, and that he died despite treatment after being admitted to the hospital.

However, alleging that Akash died due to police assault, his relatives staged continuous protests. Further, an autopsy revealed injuries at 28 places.

Police Inspector Dileepan and five other policemen were placed under suspension in connection to the death of the youth.

Subsequently, CB-CID police had been investigating the case under murder and SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, charges.

Meanwhile, the CB-CID police filed a chargesheet in the Madurai court on June 18. A copy of that chargesheet has now been received by Akash Delison’s family.

The document stated that the police took Akash to a eucalyptus grove near Manamadurai and assaulted him with an iron rod. He suffered a fracture on his right leg below the knee and above the ankle. Consequently, Akash Delison died due to a fat embolism in his blood vessels, it claimed.

‘Police hid rod used in assault’

Additionally, the chargesheet stated that the police hid the iron rod used in the assault and falsely recorded that he sustained injuries after falling while trying to escape from the police.

Six individuals — Inspector Dileepan, Sub-Inspector Guhan, and constables Kaleeswaran, Mahendran, Deiventiran, and Palaniappan — have been included as accused in this case.

‘Premeditated intent’

Akash Delison’s family alleged that the copy of the chargesheet was provided 68 days after it was filed, that it contained only 12 pages, and that all the documents recorded during the investigation were not fully provided.

The document added that the six police personnel had acted with premeditated intent, fully conscious of the victim’s caste.

World.title: 14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday.

What has happened so far:

14 babies die after fire erupts in ward; initial reports say spark erupted from AC, blaze spread due to oxygen points

Bereaved families decry rescue teams arrived “too late”; witnesses report locked doors

Health secretary removed; inquiry panel formed on PM’s orders; separate fact-finding committee constituted

Health Minister Mustafa Kamal vows accountability; Tallal Chaudhry defends district administration

Condolences from across the nation, other countries pour in

Footage showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area and grief-stricken women sitting on the ground outside the hospital. An AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility.

Several witnesses, their hands and faces blackened from the smoke, told AFP they waited hours for help from the emergency services. They were forced to smash through windows to try and get to the neonatal intensive care unit.

Others said they came across locked doors and alleged guards prevented those inside the building from leaving as the fire raged.

However, the hospital disputed this in a statement issued later in the evening. “All emergency exits were fully open and operational,” it asserted.

In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation.

“The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”.

Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said.

Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, who reached Islamabad from Karachi in the afternoon, vowed that “no one responsible for negligence, including me, will be spared”.

“The tragic fire incident at Pims MCH Centre, resulting in the loss of precious neonatal lives, is deeply heartbreaking,” the public hospital said.

Citing a preliminary report, the Pims statement said the incident was “initially caused by a spark inside nursery at 06:38am and within seconds a massive fire erupted due to oxygen points at each incubator”.

It said two doctors and two nurses on duty inside the nursery responded “immediately and called security staff, who joined in and tried to get in twice [to bring] babies out until 06:39am, when a huge blast occurred and ceilings fell down”.

The statement said the duty staff managed to rescue a baby in the nursery and four in an adjacent room, along with three mothers.

“Besides immediate response, staff managed rescue of 73 other admitted patients in the adjacent Gynae ward on the same floor within minutes,” it added.

The hospital asserted that “available fire safety equipment installed, including 35 fire extinguishers, were all utilised by the staff to contain the situation”.

Health minister vows accountability

Speaking to reporters in Islamabad, the health minister said he will present himself to his superiors for accountability.

Providing details of the incident, Kamal said: “At 6:38am, it can be seen in the CCTV footage that there was a spark in the AC, then a fireball could be seen erupting out of it and landing on the floor of the ward. In one minute, at 6:39am, four people, including two nurses and two doctors, could be seen rushing for help and around the same time, the whole room was engulfed in flames”.

The health minister said the incident was being investigated by “experts, different institutions including us”, adding that “nothing will remain hidden and all facts will be unearthed”.

He continued: “Apparently, it seems that 14 out of the 15 infants were connected to oxygen tubes and it was that oxygen which caught flame.”

Kamal reiterated that the “heart-wrenching” incident will be investigated and warned that “if there was any negligence, then as I said, we will not spare them, including myself”.

The minister further said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed him “not to speak about certain issues”. He said he would be meeting the premier and that the two had been in touch.

“Everyone is on board, and the findings will be presented,” he said.

On being asked if he was going to tender his resignation, the health minister said, “As I have said before, whoever is responsible [..] they will not be spared. I have said what I can, and I wish I could say more, but the prime minister is my boss, and whatever his orders will be, I can only say that.”

The federal minister was also questioned about fire safety standards at Pims, with a reporter pointing out that the hospital had been issued notices for the past eight years.

Kamal claimed that the hospital had ensured compliance each time a notice had been issued in the past, pointing out that the blaze was contained with “26 fire extinguishers available in the building”.

When a reporter asked about his early morning statement over the lack of adequate facilities at Pims and “why in his 2-2.5 years as a health minister, no improvement had been made”, the minister, getting visibly frustrated, said, “If it has been 2-2.5 years, then feel free to shoot me” and clarified that he had only been at his position for one year and two months.

“What I said in the morning has to be seen within a certain parameter. I was saying that even if this did not happen, there are still challenges at the hospital. It has a capacity of 200-300 OPDs, and today, it has a footfall of over 9,000 people”.

He maintained that he was merely presenting facts. “I am not saying that everything is ideal.”
