World.title: Chinese Mother Buys Daughters Extra Train Seat, Sparking Debate
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1018928/Chinese Mother Buys Daughters Extra Train Seat, Sparking Debate
World.content:
“We bought three tickets,” a teenager says to a woman asking to use the empty seat beside her — occupied by snacks — her sister sitting on the other side.

“We’re all in the same carriage,” the standing woman says. “Shouldn’t we help each other out?” She calls a train attendant for help.

“Places 5, 6, and 7 — those seats are theirs,” the attendant says after checking the teens’ tickets. “You need to talk to them about it. Telling me won’t help.”

This scene, which took place Aug. 18 on a slow train traveling from Shanghai to the southwestern city of Chengdu — a 27-hour journey — was captured in a video that went viral in China this past week.

Online, people heatedly discussed whether the girls should have shared the seat or whether they were entitled to keep it for themselves. The topic rose to the second-highest place on Chinese microblogging platform Weibo’s trending list, receiving over 37 million views and 12,000 discussions as of Monday.

Many were in support of the girls’ decision, arguing that giving up their seats would be a favor, not an obligation, as the teens themselves had paid for the three tickets. Others said that they were “wasting public resources.”

Still others contended that the train attendants should have been more proactive, pointing to railway ticketing rules that say customers can only buy one ticket for themselves per train and that if the ticket holder does not board, their seat should be reassigned by train attendants.

Despite these stipulations, passengers can buy tickets for others using their identification information on train ticket purchasing platforms.

The girls’ mother did just that, buying their tickets as well as entering her own information for the third seat, according to a now-deleted post she made on Aug. 20 on Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok.

“My original intention was to keep them from taking up other people’s space because they had too much luggage, so I bought an extra ticket,” she wrote. “Since they’re both girls and didn’t want to sit with others, I bought three tickets together.”

In response to the issue, 12306 — China’s official train ticketing and service platform — told Shanghai-based media outlet The Paper that in the event that a passenger does not board the train, their ticket remains classified as “sold” in the train’s online system. In addition, if a ticket is purchased for a passenger but they do not board, the person whose ID was used to buy the ticket retains the right to decide how the seat is used.

On Aug. 21, the Chengdu Bureau of China’s National Railway responded to the controversy, seemingly contradicting 12306: “If a passenger fails to board after purchasing a ticket due to personal reasons, the passenger is considered to have forfeited their right to use the seat … according to the rules, the seat cannot be occupied by a third party.” The bureau noted that such instances should be reported to the train staff.

But a day later, the case shifted from a dispute over passengers’ rights and entitlements to discussions on the lack of support for children traveling alone, as well as the difficulties faced by migrant families. The girls’ mother, speaking to domestic media on Aug. 22, explained that she works in Shanghai and was sending her two daughters back to their hometown. She added that she did not have enough time to escort them and wanted them to “develop their independence.” The extra seat, she said, could also serve as a place to lie down for the two, as she worried about male strangers sleeping beside them in sleeper cars.

She also noted that, under ticketing rules, minors cannot buy tickets themselves and their tickets must instead be purchased alongside an adult ticket.

In a commentary, The Paper wrote that “behind the purchase of the three tickets lies a harsh reality faced by millions of working families, leaving migrant families with no alternative.” It recommended that the railway system follow airlines — which allow parents to apply for service for unaccompanied minors in advance — as an example.

Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: A video screenshot shows the empty seat that gave rise to a national debate. From Weibo)

World.title: [Good Business] What Doris Magsaysay Ho’s recognition says about Filipino leadership
World.content:
The choice of Magsaysay Ho as recipient of the 2026 Ramon V. del Rosario Nation Building Award carries a particular meaning for women in business

When Dr. Doris Magsaysay Ho receives the Ramon V. del Rosario Award for Nation Building this year, she will make history as the first woman to receive the recognition since it was established nearly two decades ago.

That milestone deserves attention. It says something about Magsaysay Ho’s career, the industries in which she has worked, and the changing place of women in Philippine business leadership. It also raises a broader question: what does it mean to build a nation through business?

Magsaysay Ho’s career offers one answer. For decades, she has worked in an industry that connects Filipino workers to opportunities around the world while building systems that support their skills, careers, and welfare. Her work suggests that the contribution of a business leader can be measured in part by the opportunities created for people and by the capabilities they carry with them.

Magsaysay Ho inherited a family shipping business and helped develop the Magsaysay Group into a diversified organization with interests in maritime services, logistics, human resources, hospitality, and travel. The company’s growth has been accompanied by investments in training, professional development, employee welfare, and family support.

SAFE. “No deadline, no commercial gain, and no operational pressure will ever outweigh the value of the life and the well-being of our people,” says Doris Magsaysay Ho in Magsaysay Shipping and Logistics’ Make It Safe, Make It Home safety advocacy video published on the company’s Facebook page on May 19, 2026.



That focus on people is particularly relevant to the Philippine maritime industry. Filipino seafarers have long played an important role in the global maritime workforce. Behind that reputation are individuals who need access to quality training, professional opportunities, and support throughout their careers.

One example is the MOL Magsaysay Maritime Academy in Dasmariñas, Cavite, established in 2018 through a partnership between the Magsaysay Group and Mitsui O.S.K. Lines. The 13.7-hectare academy was designed to train up to 1,000 maritime students and prepare them for careers in international shipping.

An investment like this takes a long view. A student entering maritime school today may spend years developing a career that takes them across different countries and companies. The skills they acquire can support their families and contribute to an industry where the Philippines has built a strong international reputation.

The Magsaysay Group’s work with its employees reflects the same long-term thinking. Its social development arm, Homer Foundation, along with employee-led support networks such as Fundamayan and MATTERS, provides assistance in areas including health, mental wellness, financial literacy, and career advancement.

These efforts matter because employment is part of people’s lives in ways that extend beyond the workplace. A worker’s ability to stay healthy, manage finances, develop professionally, and support a family can shape the kind of career they are able to build. Businesses have a role in that environment because their decisions affect the people who spend much of their lives working within them.

Magsaysay Ho’s recognition also carries a particular meaning for women in business.

The maritime sector has historically been associated with male-dominated workplaces and leadership. Magsaysay Ho has built her career in that environment while helping create greater opportunities for women within the industry. The Magsaysay Group became the first Philippine maritime company to earn EDGE Assess certification for workplace gender equity, with women occupying 45% of its junior management roles. In 2023, Magsaysay Ho became the first woman to chair The Steamship Mutual Underwriting Association, a leading global protection and indemnity club.

FIRST. Magsaysay Group president and CEO Doris Magsaysay Ho is the first woman to chair the Steamship Mutual, one of the largest and most diverse providers of protection and indemnity (P&I) insurance globally. She took the helm in 2023. Courtesy of Magsaysay Shipping & Logistics

Her becoming the first woman recipient of the Ramon V. del Rosario Nation Building Award adds another chapter to that story.

It is worth asking why this milestone is happening only now. Women have long been part of Philippine business, working as entrepreneurs, executives, professionals, and employees across industries. Recognition at the highest levels, however, also shapes public ideas about leadership. When a woman is recognized for building an organization, creating jobs, developing people, and representing the Philippines internationally, it expands the picture of who a nation-building business leader can be.

International engagements

Magsaysay Ho’s leadership has also extended beyond the maritime industry and beyond the Philippines.

From 2006 to 2016, she represented the country in the APEC Business Advisory Council and served as its chair in 2015, when the Philippines hosted APEC. She was later awarded the Order of Gawad Mabini, Rank of Commander, for her service and contribution to advancing Philippine interests and the country’s reputation internationally.

Her work with the Asia Society Philippines Foundation has similarly brought Filipino culture and perspectives to an international audience. During her tenure as chair, the foundation helped bring Philippine heritage to New York through the “Philippine Gold: Treasures of Forgotten Kingdoms” exhibition at the Asia Society Museum.

These experiences point to another important part of Filipino leadership. The people who represent the country abroad carry more than professional expertise. They also bring their understanding of the Philippines, its people, and its possibilities into international conversations.

This connects closely with the three qualities recognized by the Ramon V. del Rosario Award for Nation Building: entrepreneurial spirit, national and global impact, and corporate citizenship and social responsibility.

Magsaysay Ho’s entrepreneurial leadership can be seen in the growth and diversification of the Magsaysay Group. Her international work has given her opportunities to represent Philippine interests in global business forums. Her work in education, employee welfare, gender inclusion, and community development reflects a sense of responsibility toward the people connected to the organization.

For me, this is what makes her recognition especially interesting. Her story provides a wider way of looking at the relationship between business and nation-building.

A successful company creates value for its owners and customers, but its influence can reach much further. It can give a young person a first opportunity, provide training that leads to a career, help a worker support a family, or give Filipino professionals the confidence and skills to compete internationally. Over time, those individual opportunities become part of a country’s economic and social story.

Magsaysay Ho’s career has been closely tied to that process.

Her being the first woman to receive the Ramon V. del Rosario Nation Building Award also gives the recognition a personal and historical dimension. She joins a group of Filipino business leaders whose work has been recognized for its contribution to the country, while opening the door wider for other women who aspire to lead.

The award will be conferred in November, coinciding with PHINMA’s 70th anniversary celebration. Its timing makes the occasion an opportunity to look back at the work that earned the recognition and to think about the kind of leadership the Philippines will need in the years ahead.

For Magsaysay Ho, that record can be traced through companies built, people trained, careers supported, opportunities created, and Filipino interests represented abroad.

That is a meaningful measure of nation-building. It is also a reminder that the future of Filipino business leadership will be shaped by the people given the opportunity to lead, the people given the opportunity to grow, and the leaders willing to invest in both. – Rappler.com

Madriella L. Mendoza is the communications officer of the PHINMA-DLSU Center for Business and Society. Ady specializes in event organization, social media strategy, and marketing. madriella.mendoza@dlsu.edu.ph.

World.title: Hundreds missing after flood hits Nepal-Tibet border, 157 bodies recovered
World.content:
Initial reports suggest an earthquake may have caused the disaster, with significant destruction to infrastructure and communities on both sides of the border

TRISHULI, Nepal – A huge wall of mud and rock collapsed into a river on the Himalayan border of Nepal and China’s Tibet on Wednesday, August 26, triggering catastrophic flooding on the Nepali side that killed scores of people and left hundreds of tourists missing.

In a still-unfolding disaster, verified videos showed dozens of people swept away at the border, with authorities on both sides fearing far higher casualties and massive destruction.

Houses, roads and power projects were washed away in Nepal, while officials in Tibet said they feared “major casualties” after a mudslide hit a border land crossing in the county of Gyirong.

“It was a huge gush of mud coming straight towards us. As it got closer, it kept rising higher and higher. When I saw it enter our home, I tried to grab my wife’s hand and take her to the terrace. But she was swept away by the mud,” said Keshav Prasad Baral, a 68-year-old survivor, who was being treated at a small hospital.

“Four or five hours later, a helicopter came to rescue me. My wife is still somewhere beneath the mud. She’s gone.”

Another survivor described being saved by clinging to a mango tree as he watched the house where he had been working disappear.

Triggered by quake?

Initial reports from Nepali officials suggested an earthquake in the area could have caused the lower part of a glacier to collapse and trigger the floods. The USGS later said the tremor recorded at the time was caused by the glacial rock and ice collapsing to the valley floor.

As darkness fell, authorities continued the grim task of recovering and trying to identify bodies.

Some 157 bodies had been recovered so far, Nepal police said late on Wednesday.

Officials at Nepal’s tourism ministry told media outlets that over 400 tourists are missing, of whom around 340 are foreigners.

Sunil Sharma, a Nepal tourism board spokesperson, told the Associated Press that 133 of the tourists were from India on a pilgrimage.

He said 47 of the missing tourists were from the United States, 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 24 from Canada.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said UN teams and partners were mobilizing supplies and personnel in Nepal to support communities affected by the disaster.

A US State Department spokesperson said: “The State Department is aware of Americans impacted by the floods in Nepal and is closely tracking the situation.”

Canada was also closely following the situation, said Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on X, calling the floods “absolutely devastating.”

The region lies on a popular route to Kailash Manasarovar in Tibet, a site visited annually by hundreds of Hindu pilgrims from India and elsewhere, particularly at this time of year.

China’s state broadcaster said three people were killed and 265 missing in Gyirong. It said the toll was still being verified and rescue efforts were ongoing.

South Korea separately said that eight of its nationals working on a hydropower plant were missing.

People fleeing

Security footage captured on the Chinese side of the Nepal-Tibet border showed many people fleeing before a torrent of rock, mud and water destroyed buildings and vehicles and took many lives.

The German Research Centre for Geosciences said there was a 4.4-magnitude quake approximately seven minutes before the time shown on the security footage time-stamp.

Locals from the affected areas of Nuwakot and Dhading were seen gathering outside a Nepali army training center – the base for helicopter rescue operations – seeking information about missing family members.

Police were recording the names of the missing just outside the barracks gate, using mobile phone flashlights as their only source of light as the area remained without electricity due to damaged hydropower infrastructure.

In the affected areas, houses, trees and vehicles were submerged or buried in mudslides. Helicopters hovered overhead all day in the area bringing in survivors.

An initial study of Planet Labs satellite imagery indicated that a landslide of ice and rock triggered a debris-laden flood in the Lhende River, about 20 km northeast of the Nepal-China Rasuwagadhi border crossing, Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said on X.

Rescue helicopters could not land in Nepal’s affected areas of Syapru Besi and Timure in the mountainous district of Rasuwa, with a population of about 50,000, officials said, with the river flowing above its normal course.

Television images showed collapsed homes, floating cars and a metal bridge being washed away, while witnesses told Reuters the waters engulfed entire villages.

“There is devastation everywhere we look,” Tula Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa, told Reuters. “The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing.”

Gyirong port affected

China’s official Xinhua news agency said the mudslide hit the Gyirong port, cutting roads, communications and power links in the Shigatse region near the border.

A rescuer interviewed by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV said they had been trying to establish contact with the Gyirong border port but “so far there haven’t been any results”. All roads leading to the border crossing had been “completely destroyed” after a preliminary inspection with a drone, the rescuer added.

With the deluge of muddy water sweeping down from an estimated nearly 2,000 meters (6,560 feet) above sea level, flood alerts were issued in the populous northern Indian states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, which border Nepal and where several rivers flow down the mountains into the plains.

Authorities in Bihar said they had evacuated about 5,000 people from six districts and planned to evacuate a total of 10,000 to 12,000 people. – Rappler.com

World.title: 2 firms behind TRO on P85 metro wage hike raked in billions in DPWH deals
World.content:
PROTEST. The Unity for Wage Increase Now (UWIN), a coalition of labor groups, marched in front of the Department of Labor and Employment headquarters to denounce the agency's failure to ensure the implementation of the P85 daily minimum wage increase, on August 7, 2026.

Because of the temporary restraining order, minimum wage earners in Metro Manila have effectively been deprived of P1,560 each, says labor leader Sonny Matula

The two companies behind the petition to put on hold the long-awaited P85 wage hike in Metro Manila bagged billions worth of contracts from the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH).

Based on Rappler’s analysis of DPWH contracts, Readycon Trading and Construction Corporation cornered P9.07 billion worth of contracts from 2016 to 2026.

Meanwhile, R-II Builders secured P3.3 billion worth of DPWH contracts from 2019 to 2022. Of this, three contracts with a total cost of P503.3 million were a joint venture between R-II Builders and Arconic Inc.

Following the two companies’ petition, Pasig Regional Trial Court’s Branch 152 issued a temporary restraining order (TRO) against the regional wage board and the National Wages and Productivity Commission, pulling the brakes on the wage hike.

They argued that the abrupt increase would disrupt projects priced before the wage order was issued. Readycon estimated an immediate additional payroll expense of around P409,257 attributable to the minimum wage increase alone.

“Paanong malulugi itong mga kompanyang ito kung coming from secretary of DPWH, they were able to secure billions pesos of contracts and yet they cannot pay their workers a measly P60 increase from the P85 na dagdag sahod ng mga manggagawa?” Kamanggagawa Representative Eli San Fernando said during the House budget hearing of DPWH on Wednesday, August 26.

(How can these companies claim they are losing money when, according to the DPWH secretary, they were able to secure billions’ worth of contracts, yet they cannot afford to pay their workers even a measly P60 increase out of the P85 wage hike granted to workers?)

The first P60 tranche had already taken effect on July 25, raising the daily minimum wage for non-agricultural workers from P695 to P755. An additional P25 had been scheduled for January 20, 2027, which would have brought the rate up to P780.

Companies’ sketchy background

DPWH Secretary Vince Dizon said Readycon is the “number one” company in asphalt and road construction.

In early August, however, Dizon expressed dismay after seeing portions of EDSA riddled with potholes shortly after Readycon rehabilitated the road. The damage emerged following heavy rain brought by the southwest monsoon or habagat.

Dizon said Readycon had already repaired the potholes.

In 2014, the Commission on Audit flagged Readycon over defects in the C-5 Extension project.

According to Readycon’s website, the company was founded in 1988 and holds a Quadruple A (AAAA) license from the Philippine Contractors Accreditation Board.

Aside from the DPWH, Readycon has also secured government contracts from the Manila International Airport Authority, Philippine Ports Authority, National Housing Authority, and city and municipal engineering offices.

Court documents identify Jesus Ignacio as the company’s president.

Meanwhile, Rappler’s investigation published in April found that R-II Builders was involved in a subcontracting scheme.

Documents the company filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission in 2025 show that R-II Builders is owned by Reghis Romero II, the father of former 1-Pacman party-list representative Mikee Romero.

However, court documents related to the wage hike identify a certain Carlos B. Carlos as the president of R-II Builders.

Labor Code violation?

Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino said the department was saddened by the decision but would respect the court’s ruling.

“Malungkot ako para sa mga manggagawa pero susunod tayo sa utos ng husgado,” Tolentino said in a statement. (I feel sad for the workers, but we will abide by the court’s order.)

Senate committee on labor and employment Chairperson Joel Villanueva and Vice Chairperson Raffy Tulfo, meanwhile, questioned the legality of the issuance of a TRO for the wage hike.

“No preliminary or permanent injunction or temporary restraining order may be issued by any court, tribunal or other entity against proceedings before the Commission or the Regional Boards,” Article 126 of the Labor Code reads.

The Federation of Free Workers (FFW) also questioned the validity of the TRO.

“Hindi namin sinasabing bawal magreklamo ang employer. Ang sinasabi namin, may tamang forum ang reklamo. Hindi homeless ang wage dispute. May address na ibinigay ang batas,” FFW President Sonny Matula said.

(We are not saying that employers are prohibited from filing a complaint. What we are saying is that there is a proper forum for such complaints. Wage disputes are not homeless. The law has designated where they should be addressed.)

Because of the TRO, minimum wage earners in Metro Manila have effectively been deprived of P1,560 each, Matula said in a statement on Tuesday, August 25. – with reports from Lance Spencer Yu/Rappler.com

World.title: Tim Curry, actor famed for ‘Rocky Horror Picture Show,’ dies at 80
World.content:
Curry's best-known role was Dr. Frank N. Furter, which came in his debut film, the outrageous, crowd-pleasing horror-comedy-musical 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show,' co-starring Susan Sarandon and Barry Bostwick

Tim Curry, the baritone-voiced British actor who pranced to movie fame as a singing, lingerie-clad “sweet transvestite” in the 1975 cult classic The Rocky Horror Picture Show, has died at the age of 80, his manager said on Wednesday, August 26.

A cause of death was not immediately given, but Curry had been in ill health for some time. He died peacefully on Tuesday at his home in Los Angeles, his manager said.

Curry appeared in numerous movies, often as a hammy villain, was nominated three times for a Tony Award for Broadway roles, and performed voice work in many animated films and TV shows.

But his best-known role was Dr. Frank N. Furter, which came in his debut film, the outrageous, crowd-pleasing horror-comedy-musical The Rocky Horror Picture Show, co-starring Susan Sarandon and Barry Bostwick.

“I’m not much of a man by the light of day. But by night I’m one hell of a lover. I’m just a sweet transvestite from transsexual Transylvania,” Curry sang in one scene as he strutted around with garish eye shadow and lipstick, in a skimpy black outfit complete with black stockings and garter belt.

In a 1975 television interview, Curry noted the risk of having his career defined by such an outlandish role — a prescient worry, as it turned out. “When I read it, I just thought it was very, very witty and funny,” Curry said, although he confessed to some initial reluctance.

“I mean, I was hesitant in that, if it worked, it might be a difficult thing to shake off. But, really, I’ve always thought that it (a part) wasn’t worth doing unless you took a risk,” Curry said.

Among his other films were Charlie’s Angels (2000), Muppet Treasure Island (1996), The Shadow (1994), The Three Musketeers (1993), Home Alone 2: Lost in New York (1992), Clue (1985), Legend (1985) and Annie (1982).

Over-the-top villains

OVER-THE-TOP VILLAINS

Curry did much of his best work on stage. He was nominated for a Tony, Broadway’s top honor, in 1981 for his role as Mozart in Amadeus, a tale of the great composer’s interaction with jealous rival Salieri. Curry was also nominated for a Tony in 1993 for My Favorite Year and in 2005 for his role as King Arthur in the zany Monty Python’s Spamalot.

Possessing a rich baritone voice, he was in demand as a voice actor for animated films and TV shows. He won a Daytime Emmy Award in 1991 for his voice work on the animated Peter Pan & the Pirates.

With his sinister grin and menacing laugh, Curry was frequently cast in Hollywood films as a villain — sometimes with comic overtones, which let him deliver the type of over-the-top performances for which he was famed.

“I do love those roles — they’re always the best written,” Curry told interviewer Andrew Kay in 2011.

He conceded that some of his movies were mediocre, singling out 1995’s “Congo,” a tale of diamond mines and killer gorillas.

“I was really very bad in it,” Curry said. “I won a Razzy award for one of the worst performances of the year – and I richly deserved it, too.”

A cult following

Curry was born in the English village of Grappenhall, Cheshire, on April 19, 1946. His father, a Royal Navy chaplain, died when he was 12. His mother was a school secretary.

Curry studied drama at Birmingham University.

In 1973, he landed the part of Dr. Frank N. Furter in the original London stage version of The Rocky Horror Show. He performed the play in New York and Los Angeles before it was made into a film, renamed as The Rocky Horror Picture Show.

The movie was not an instant hit but won a cult following in midnight screenings in New York City and elsewhere, with audience members often dressing up as Rocky Horror characters.

Curry withdrew from a British stage production in 2011 due to ill health. In 2013, his agent said that he had suffered a stroke but was recovering “in great humor.” From then on he used a wheelchair and reduced his workload. In 2024, he did, however, return to the big screen, appearing in the horror film Stream.

Curry, who lived in Los Angeles, never married and had no children. A composer and a singer, Curry also performed with his own rock band and released a handful of albums. – Rappler.com

World.title: Meta reaches $16.68-billion settlement over social media harms to children
World.content:
META. The logo of Meta at the Meta Lab in Los Angeles, California, US, on May 20, 2026.

(1st UPDATE) Meta will impose daily usage limits and restrict nighttime usage by children who use Facebook and Instagram, and enhance measures to prevent children from accessing age-restricted content

Meta Platforms agreed to pay a maximum $16.68 billion and make major changes to Facebook and Instagram to resolve claims by states across the US that the company designed those platforms to addict children, misled consumers about their safety and improperly collected children’s personal data.

The settlement resolves claims brought by 29 US states, and will end a federal trial that had been one of the highest-profile tests yet of allegations that social media companies harmed young users.

Meta will impose daily usage limits and restrict nighttime usage by children who use Facebook and Instagram, and enhance measures to prevent children from accessing age-restricted content.

The Menlo Park, California-based company denied wrongdoing in agreeing to settle.

Wednesday’s settlement also resolves lawsuits by California, Illinois, New Mexico and Washington, D.C., over privacy claims related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, where the consulting firm collected personal data of millions of Facebook users. Those states will receive $459.3 million to resolve those lawsuits.

Shares of Meta rose 2.3% in early trading.

The claims were part of a broader wave of litigation brought by states, local governments, school districts and individuals alleging that Meta and other social media companies fueled a nationwide youth mental health crisis.

The trial in the Oakland, California, federal court covered claims from California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey that Meta violated their state laws protecting consumers.

It also covered claims from 29 states that Meta ⁠violated the federal Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act by collecting personal data from users it knew were children without parental notification or consent, and using the data to train machine learning and generative AI models.

Meta has long argued it could not have misled consumers about whether its services were addictive because “social media addiction” is not a recognized psychiatric condition.

Before the trial began on August 18, Meta said California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey were seeking up to $1.4 trillion in penalties. The states suggested that the figure would be closer to $200 billion.

A mental health crisis

Meta, Snapchat and its parent Snap, YouTube and its parent Alphabet, and TikTok and its parent ByteDance still face thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts over claims they knowingly designed their platforms to have features that addict children and teenagers, fueling a mental health crisis. A trial in Nashville over claims brought by Tennessee against Meta began last month.

The federal cases were consolidated before US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland, and include lawsuits brought by individuals, school districts and state governments.

Earlier this year, Meta lost both phases of a landmark lawsuit brought by New Mexico. A jury in March ordered it to pay $375 million after finding it had misled consumers about the safety of its platforms. On August 6, a judge found Meta had created a public nuisance and ordered it to pay an additional $567 million and implement youth-safety measures.

Also in March, the first trial over an individual’s claims against Meta and Google ended with a verdict in the plaintiff’s favor. A Los Angeles jury found the companies liable for plaintiff Kaley G.M.’s depression and anxiety and ordered them to pay a combined $6 million in damages.

The companies have said they will appeal those verdicts. – Rappler.com

World.title: Sara Duterte trial: Prosecution navigates minefield after sub judice ruling
World.content:
MANILA, Philippines – After the impeachment court laid out clearer sanctions against violators of the sub judice rule on Wednesday, August 26., the prosecution panel has been more careful than ever.

No public or private prosecutor faced House-organized press conferences, while some gave relatively few words during chance interviews.

“Personally, I will behave,” private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said.

The ruling read by presiding officer Chiz Escudero promised public reprimand for first-time offenders of Rule 18 of the impeachment rules handbook, and a fine of P30,000 for every succeeding offense. The said provision prohibits senator-judges, prosecutors, the respondent, and their defense team from commenting on the merits of the case outside the court.

While the penalties apply not only to the prosecution but also to the defense, it is not difficult to surmise that the House side is whom Escudero is referring to when he says one party has violated the sub judice rule more than the other.

When Escudero read remarks the court found problematic, most of the soundbites came from prosecutors, such as Jay Tolosa, Amando Virgil Ligutan, Mae Divinagracia, and Terry Ridon.

Wednesday’s ruling was triggered by defense lawyer Sheila Sison’s previous move to call out Ligutan for posting on Facebook that misleading questions are not allowed even during cross-examinations. The comment was an apparent reaction to the claim made by defense lawyer Kristine Ferrer before the court.

Before Escudero issued his ruling, Ligutan was given the opportunity to deliver his counter-manifestation, in which he insisted he did not violate the court’s sub judice rule.

“To the defense, the post is not about you. It is not personal. It is about the law that we all adhere to. It is about what we teach the public who are watching our trial. Correcting a mistake is never wrong. Doing it while a hearing is ongoing, online, does not make it not right,” Ligutan added.

Play Video

Press briefing sans prosecutors

As the impact of the ruling reverberates, the House opted not to let a member of the prosecution team face the media for its regular lunch break and post-trial press conferences on Wednesday.

Instead, the media relied on soundbites of prosecution spokesman Zia Alonto Adiong, and deputy speakers Paolo Ortega, Janette Garin, and Jay Khonghun. For Rappler’s special coverage, we were able to book Manila 6th District Representative Benny Abante, one of the endorsers of the impeachment complaint that became the basis of the impeachment articles transmitted to the Senate.

Play Video

“(The sub judice rule) should also extend to the respondent,” Adiong said. “Whatever she says should also be guided by the sub judice rule…(such as her statement on the impeachment process) ‘bending the law,'” Adiong said.

Duterte’s statement in early August — an apparent swipe at the House and the impeachment court — was notably absent from Escudero’s examples of remarks that violated the sub judice rule.

While Escudero was delivering his speech, Duterte in fact issued another statement calling out the prosecution for calling her a scam mastermind, and senator-judge Raffy Tulfo for describing her special disbursing officer Gina Acosta as “stupid.”

Lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro later informed the court about Duterte’s latest remarks. Escudero said the enforcement of new sanctions will apply prospectively, giving her the same clean slate as prosecutors who made the statements flagged by the court.

Absolute prohibition?

Prosecutors Kapunan, Ridon, and Tolosa said they respect the court’s decision, although the ruling creates a more complicated communications terrain.

The prosecution team, for one, has to discuss whether Tolosa stays on as its spokesperson. The defense team already said it is looking for a new talking head as defense lawyer Michael Poa seeks to relinquish the post.

Play Video

“Perhaps we need some clarification regarding the order, because it sounded like an absolute prohibition to talk about matters that may touch on the merits of the case. There’s an exemption to that sub judice ruling under jurisprudence which is the doctrine of true, fair, and accurate reporting. If you’re just quoting what has already been stated by the witness in an open court…that shall not be a violation of the sub judice rule,” Tolosa said.

“This is not a regular trial. It is a political, constitutional, and legal process. It is very different from the proceedings prescribed in regular courts,” Ridon added.

The new rules appear to constrain the defense less than the prosecution, which bears the burden of proof while also seeking to win the court of public opinion, as the sui generis trial — a proceeding that is a class of its own — unfolds.

“That’s a very eloquent way of issuing a gag order,” constitutional lawyer Lulu Reyes told Rappler.

Play Video

– Rappler.com
